title: What If Emperor Penguins Ran Out of Ice?

scenes.text: What if emperor penguins ran out of ice to breed on? In 2022, four colonies already did.
Emperors raise chicks on sea ice that must hold through the winter. In one Antarctic region, it didn't.
In the Bellingshausen Sea, the ice did not form until late June, when the birds should already have been incubating eggs.
By December, the central and eastern part of that sea had lost all its sea ice. Chicks without ice risk drowning.
Four of the five colonies in the region, all found by satellite, probably lost every chick.
From 2018 to 2022, 30 percent of the 62 known colonies lost ice. By 2100, over 90 percent could be quasi-extinct.
